text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Philips Electronics' finance director and executive vice-president Dudley Eustace promoted to vice-chairman. (p1)
- Entertainment company Endemol cancels plans to invest Dfl 40 million in two theatres, two hotels and a ballroom in south-east Amsterdam. (p1)
- Difference between income brackets in Netherlands grew eight percent in 20 years. (p1)
- Banks to provide clients with investment information by GSM-phones and buzzers. (p1)
- Active coal maker and personal care group Norit posts 68 pct higher 1996 net, expects continuing turnover and profit growth. (p3)
- Brewer Heineken misses chance to buy car maker Volvo's 55 pct stake in Scandinavia's largest brewer, Pripps Ringnes. (p3)
- Temp agency Content Beheer reports 22 percent increase in 1996 profit, in pace with market growth. (p3)
- Grolsch starts study into optimising production at Groenlo and Deventer breweries. (p4)
VOLKSKRANT
- Environment Minister opposes accord on Schiphol airport's future reached between her civil servants and those of the economic and traffic ministry. (p1)
- Three more farms contaminated by swine fever in province of Brabant. (p1)
- Defence apparatus maker Holland Signaal has trouble finding suitable staff. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Violent confrontation between Ajax and Feyenoord supporters on Amsterdam circular road. (p1)
- Delegation of Malaysian state company Khazanah Nasional Berahd visits Netherlands to talk about bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker's restart. (p13)
- Joint employers reject any fiscal attack on car users as attempt to fight traffic jams. (p13)
- Britain's central bank president Eddy George supports Wim Duisenberg's candidacy for European central bank post. (p13)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Temp agencies lose market share due to sector's organisations creating own secondment bureaus. (p13)
TROUW
- PM Wim Kok promises to give aged pensioners extra money a half year earlier. (p1)
- Schiphol airport and Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM quarrel over air traffic growth. (p3)
